recent_posts.title: First Rails app shipped to the App Store without Xcode using Ruby Native
recent_posts.summary: Joe Masilotti, a developer who has spent 10+ years helping Rails teams ship iOS apps, shares the story behind launching Ruby Native — a tool that lets Rails developers publish to the App Store without ever opening Xcode. The post recounts the painful gauntlet of Apple provisioning, certificates, and App Store Connect that blocks most Rails developers from going mobile, and celebrates the first customer app (Foxance) shipped entirely through Ruby Native by a developer in South Africa who never interacted with Xcode or with Joe himself.

recent_posts.title: The Rails developers' guide to mobile app frameworks
recent_posts.summary: Rails developers have four main options for building mobile apps: fully native (Swift/Kotlin) offers the best experience but requires three codebases and dedicated mobile teams; React Native provides cross-platform development but still requires a separate frontend; PWAs are fastest to build but lack app store presence; and Hotwire Native wraps existing Rails apps in native shells, letting one team maintain web and mobile with minimal native code. The choice depends on team composition, timeline, offline requirements, and whether app store presence is essential.

recent_posts.title: Hotwire Native at Rails World
recent_posts.summary: Joe Masilotti's newsletter covers his upcoming keynote on Hotwire Native at Rails World 2025, the launch of Ruby Friends Android app for conference networking, and a tutorial on creating native-feeling modals. The newsletter also highlights community developments including 37signals' Action Native Push gem for mobile notifications, technical deep-dives into Hotwire Native's architecture, and the Rails World 2025 conference app built with Hotwire Native.

recent_posts.title: RailsConf workshop recording and Ruby Friends v1.2
recent_posts.summary: A newsletter update covering the release of a RailsConf Hotwire Native workshop recording on YouTube, a tutorial on adding native buttons to Hotwire Native apps using bridge components, and the launch of Ruby Friends v1.2 with new iOS features including QR code scanning, push notifications, Universal Links, and Apple Wallet integration. The author also mentions working on NFC integration and plans to extract reusable components for their bridge component library.

recent_posts.title: Ruby Friends is in the App Store!
recent_posts.summary: Ruby Friends, a networking app for Ruby developers, launched in the App Store after 12 days of development. The app helps conference attendees connect by sharing profiles via QR codes, with no social media features - just simple friend connections. It reached 100 profiles within 48 hours and now has over 250 users. Built using Hotwire Native and Ruby on Rails, the development process was streamed live on YouTube, covering iOS app setup, tab bar implementation, and sign-in flow integration.

recent_posts.title: RailsConf inspired me to build something new
recent_posts.summary: A developer reflects on attending the final RailsConf, sharing insights from conversations with other developers about pricing strategies, Hotwire Native success stories, and book publishing. The post covers a workshop on building iOS and Android apps with Hotwire Native, highlights talks on authentication and PWAs, and announces a new project called Ruby Friends - a networking app for Ruby developers to connect at conferences and maintain relationships afterward.

recent_posts.title: Hotwire Native at RailsConf
recent_posts.summary: Joe Masilotti announces his Hotwire Native workshop at RailsConf, where attendees will build iOS and Android apps from scratch using Ruby on Rails without needing Swift or Kotlin knowledge. The workshop covers building maintainable cross-platform apps with a thin wrapper approach that enables continuous deployment across all platforms. He also mentions a book meet-up for his Hotwire Native for Rails Developers book with exclusive discount codes and giveaways.

recent_posts.title: Hotwire Native v1.2.x and Hotwire Native LIVE #4
recent_posts.summary: Hotwire Native released patch versions 1.2.1 for iOS and 1.2.3 for Android, marking the first time platforms diverged on release numbers. Android v1.2.3 adds better error messaging for out-of-date browsers and programmatic tab bar control for feature parity with iOS. iOS v1.2.1 introduces queryStringPresentation configuration for better URL navigation handling and restores iOS 15 support. The update also covers upcoming RailsConf workshop content and explores Route Decision Handlers for customizing navigation behavior between URLs.

recent_posts.title: iOS 26, Hotwire Native LIVE #3, and a new bridge component
recent_posts.summary: Apple's iOS 26 introduces Liquid Glass design system, which automatically benefits Hotwire Native apps without requiring code changes. Unlike React Native, Hotwire Native uses first-party iOS components directly, ensuring seamless integration with new system designs. The update includes debugging techniques for Hotwire Native apps and introduces a new Theme Component for keeping system UI synchronized with web-based designs.

recent_posts.title: Book sale, Hotwire Native LIVE #2, and Hotwire Native around the web
recent_posts.summary: Joe Masilotti's newsletter highlights the second Hotwire Native LIVE episode focusing on bridge components, a 40% discount on his Hotwire Native book through Pragmatic Bookshelf's spring sale, and community articles covering seamless loading techniques and custom Android keyboard extensions for Hotwire Native apps.

top_posts.title: Turbo Native is dead, long live Hotwire Native!
top_posts.summary: Hotwire Native has officially replaced Turbo Native, making mobile development easier for Rails developers by combining Turbo Native and Strada into a unified package with improved APIs and documentation. The iOS library was developed by the 37signals team, and the new setup allows seamless navigation between native and web screens. The author is also working on a book titled 'Hotwire Native for Rails Developers,' anticipating a public beta release soon.

top_posts.title: Idea to App Store in 7 days
top_posts.summary: The author built a web and iOS app called Daily Log in 7 days to track exercise, water intake, food, medications, and supplements. The web app was built using Ruby on Rails and the iOS app used Turbo Native. The author faced a challenge when Apple didn't like the idea that the app required an account, but they eventually approved it for the App Store. The entire codebase is open source.

top_posts.title: Hotwire Native book, in beta!
top_posts.summary: The Hotwire Native book for Rails developers is now available in beta. It provides insights on building hybrid apps for web, iOS, and Android, emphasizing a server-driven approach. The book covers the advantages of native components, best practices for mobile SDKs and APIs, and pitfalls to avoid. Purchasers of the beta will receive the final version upon release and can contribute feedback for improvements.

top_posts.summary: Comparison of using gems, recipes, and generators for authentication in Rails.

top_posts.title: Turbo Native iOS and Android apps in 15 minutes
top_posts.summary: Turbo Native allows Ruby on Rails developers to build iOS and Android apps easily. This tutorial provides step-by-step instructions on how to build basic Turbo Native apps from scratch using Swift and Kotlin. By the end of the tutorial, the reader will have iOS and Android apps powered by Turbo Native that implement basic integration features.
